content: Standard forecasting accuracy metrics: MASE (scale-free, Hyndman 2006, values <1 beat naive, stable on zero series) is the single most recommended metric for cross-series comparison. sMAPE (bounded 0-200%, symmetric, used in M competitions) is widely used but has edge-case issues near zero. RMSE (scale-dependent, sensitive to outliers) needed when same-unit interpretation matters. MAE (robust to outliers, scale-dependent). OWA = 0.5*(MASE/MASE_Naive2 + sMAPE/sMAPE_Naive2) was the M4 primary ranking metric combining both. MSIS (Mean Scaled Interval Score) = scaled version of Winkler interval score, rewards narrow intervals + good coverage, used in M4 probabilistic track, formula: (1/h)*sum[(U_t-L_t) + (2/alpha)(L_t-Y_t)*1(Y_t<L_t) + (2/alpha)(Y_t-U_t)*1(Y_t>U_t)] / in-sample naive error. RMSSE (Root Mean Squared Scaled Error) introduced for M5 competition with intermittent/zero-heavy demand data. CRPS = integral of pinball loss over all quantiles, proper scoring rule for full predictive distributions.
